title: Duplicate or clone entries
description: This check finds lexical entries that say the same thing twice. Entries are compared by their hyphen-trimmed form and morph type class. Two kinds of group are reported. A duplicate group holds entries whose gloss sets and MSA signatures (kind, categories with their from and to roles, and slots) are equal. A clone group is one clone entry listed first, followed by only the same-form homographs whose glosses it extends: every gloss of the clone is a gloss of that homograph plus a dotted suffix, or the capitalised form plus a dotted suffix, a clone made only to carry a feature. Each clone is its own group, so two clones of one entry give two findings. A clone whose glosses are all the capitalised form plus a dotted suffix names no homograph, so its group holds the clone alone. Entries whose lexeme form has no form text, such as a reduplication entered twice, are grouped by morph type class, glosses and MSA signature alone.
